channel.title: The Catholic Review - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Catholic Review (catholicreview.org)

item.title: From discipleship to apostleship: SEEK promises encounter with Christ that continues
item.description: FOCUS announced SEEK 2027 will take place Jan. 1-5 in two cities that have hosted it before: San Antonio and Columbus, Ohio. The local bishops, Archbishop Gustavo García-Siller of San Antonio and Bishop Earl K. Fernandes of Columbus, welcomed the news.

item.title: St. Carlo Acutis Camping Retreat builds faith in the great outdoors
item.description: Youths ages 5 to 17 who are involved with outdoor troops such as Scouting America, Trail Life, American Heritage Girls, Camp Fire, Troops of St. George and the Federation of North American Explorers are invited, along with their families, to the retreat April 17-19, which will be held for the first time at the O’Dwyer Retreat Center in Sparks.

item.title: ‘Operation Metro Surge’ in Minneapolis is ending but needs continue for immigrant families
item.description: Redemptorist Father John Schmidt, pastor of St. Alphonsus in Brooklyn Center, was cautiously optimistic as he heard the news Feb. 12 that "Operation Metro Surge" was nearing an end.

item.title: Bioethics of the brain: A conversation with a Catholic neurosurgeon
item.description: Charlie Camosy recently spoke on this topic with Gabriel LeBeau, a second-year neurosurgery resident at the University of Kansas Medical Center, who has had the bioethics of the brain on his mind for a while now with an interest in brain-machine interfaces, neurotechnology and cerebrovascular neurosurgery.

item.title: Bishop Zurek resignation accepted; Cardinal DiNardo named as apostolic administrator of Amarillo
item.description: Pope Leo XIV has accepted the resignation of Bishop Patrick J. Zurek of Amarillo, 77, and has appointed retired Cardinal Daniel N. DiNardo, 76, as apostolic administrator of the diocese until a new bishop is appointed and installed.

item.title: Federal judge orders Catholic group be let into ICE facility on Ash Wednesday
item.description: A federal district judge granted a preliminary injunction Feb. 12 that will allow clergy, religious and Catholic social justice advocates to enter a Immigration and Customs Enforcement facility west of Chicago on Ash Wednesday to provide ashes and holy Communion.

item.title: Radio Interview: Archbishop Lori’s pastoral letter: ‘In Charity and Truth’
item.description: In a new pastoral letter released Feb. 9, Archbishop William E. Lori of Baltimore takes the occasion of the nation’s 250th anniversary to address “a moment of grace and responsibility.” Catholic Review Editor Christopher Gunty talked with the archbishop about the motivation for the letter, which is subtitled, “Toward a Renewed Political Culture.”

item.title: A true parish welcomes everyone, spreads respect, harmony, pope says
item.description: An authentic Christian community knows how to sincerely and joyfully welcome everyone: Catholics, non-Catholics and people of no faith at all, Pope Leo XIV said.

item.title: Latin Mass supporters say SSPX controversy has ‘thrown a hand grenade’ into TLM debate
item.description: Supporters of the traditional Latin Mass have urged Catholics not to confuse their movement with the more controversial Society of St. Pius X, commonly referred to as SSPX, whose leaders currently risk excommunication by threatening to ordain their own bishops.

item.title: Mount St. Joseph’s BJ Ransom selected as BCL Player of Year; league unveils new academic honors
item.description: Mount St. Joseph senior guard BJ Ranson, who led the Gaels to a 29-win regular season, earned the Baltimore Catholic League’s Jerry Savage Player of the Year Award for the 2025-26 season.
